actions.name: Occurs in at least one protected area

documentation.range: This species was previously known from Europe (excluding Ireland and most Mediterranean islands [though it is present on Sicily]), and northern Eurasia, with subpopulations in Türkiye and north Africa (Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia). However, following genetic analysis, it no longer occurs in Jersey, western and southern France, Andorra, the Iberian Peninsula, Morocco, northern Algeria and extreme northwestern Tunisia, as these records have now been assigned to Bufo spinosus which has been elevated from subspecies level (Recuero et al. 2012). In Europe, it is present in most areas (including the United Kingdom, Norway, Sweden and Finland), ranging as far eastwards as Xinjiang, China, northern Kazakhstan and eastern Siberia. In the Middle East, it is found north and west of Türkiye. It occurs between sea level to 3,000 m asl, however, in northern portions of the range the species occurs at much lower elevations.
documentation.population: Although this species is generally common over much of its range, some localized major declines have been observed. It is suspected to be decreasing in Bulgaria (Y. Kornilev, G. Popgeorgiev and B. Naumov pers. comm. October 2019). In Czechia, this species has declined from thousands of individuals to hundreds in the last 10–20 years (A. Krása pers comm. September 2019). This may have occurred due to the intensification of fish farming and the increase in predator species (A. Krása pers comm. September 2019). Major declines have also been observed in Italy in the last 10 years (F. Ficetola and R. Manenti pers. comm. September 2019), the Netherlands (R. Zollinger pers. comm. September 2019), and United Kingdom (J. Wilkinson pers. comm. September 2019). These declines may be due to threats such as habitat loss, road mortalities etc. and/or a combination, but some also appear to be enigmatic and occurring in areas where the habitat is fine (Europe Red List Assessment Workshop September 2019).
documentation.habitats: This is a widespread and adaptable species present in coniferous, mixed and deciduous forests, groves, bushlands, meadows, arid areas, parks and gardens. It is usually in damp areas with dense vegetation, and large open areas are generally avoided. The species spawns and larval development takes place in still waters and slow-moving parts of rivers and streams. It is present in many modified habitats.
documentation.threats:
There are generally no major threats to this widespread and common species. Subpopulations might be locally impacted through deforestation, drainage of wetlands, pollution, agricultural intensification, urbanization, desertification, mortality on roads (migrating animals), and persecution. In parts of the former Soviet Union it is collected in small numbers for the pet trade. This species can be affected by the increase of UV-B radiation (Lizana and Pedraza 1998). In the United Kingdom the species is increasingly suffering from habitat fragmentation and some unexplained declines have occurred.

Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis (Bd), which causes the disease chytridiomycosis, is a potential threat to the species and has been reported in some UK subpopulations. This may also be a possibility for the enigmatic declines observed in the UK, Italy and the Netherlands, although these declines are poorly understood and further research would be required to confirm this.
documentation.measures:
Conservation Actions In-Place
This species is present in numerous protected areas, is listed on Appendix III of the Bern Convention, and is protected by national and sub-national legislation in many countries. It is recorded on many national and sub-national Red Data books and lists. In parts of this species' range, mitigation measures to reduce road kill have been established.

Research Needed
Population monitoring is required, as well as research to understand the cause of declines observed in this species across its range.
documentation.use_trade: This species is collected for the pet trade and used for food at a subsistence and national level.
documentation.rationale: Listed as Least Concern in view of its wide distribution, tolerance of a broad range of habitats, presumed large population, and because it is unlikely to be declining fast enough for listing in a more threatened category.
documentation.taxonomic_notes:
This is a restricted concept of this species following the splits of the broader concept into this and Bufo spinosus (García-Porta et al. 2012, Recuero et al. 2012).

Following genetic analysis, parts of the former range of this species (e.g. Jersey, western and southern France, Andorra, and the Iberian Peninsula) have been assigned to Bufo spinosus which has been elevated from subspecies level (García-Porta et al. 2012, Recuero et al. 2012).
